scope: Uniform Actor scale: projection predicates, concrete Motion type9 formats and hidden Float32 ABI arguments
decision: Preserve the positive scalar proposal, but do not publish a timed Tiny/Giant reward yet. Complete the bounded root-motion resource contract and per-actor cleanup journal first.

claims.Finding: Builds scaled Actor+64, then composes root-motion translation/rotation into Actor+2056. Both root-motion calls pass XMM2=-1.0, selecting the current motion frame. Floor alignment and a custom callback are additional branches.
claims.Limitations: Complete ASM; a readable current matrix alone does not bound a future composed matrix.

claims.Finding: Actor+2488 bit8 selects the Euler orientation branch.
claims.Limitations: The other branch constructs and normalizes a basis from the direction vector.

claims.Finding: Builds axis rotations from the three Euler components and composes them using the common Float32 matrix routines.
claims.Limitations: No added finite-value guard is inferred.

claims.Finding: Floor alignment derives basis vectors from two resource/contact points and normalizes them before the caller reapplies scale.
claims.Limitations: This branch is excluded from the initial simple projection proposal until its inputs are bounded.

claims.Finding: Checks Actor+2488 bit1, Actor+288 bit1 clear and absence of attachment for the ordinary floor-alignment branch.
claims.Limitations: One part of the full caller predicate.

claims.Finding: Consults decoded Actor+12 resource flags and Actor flags+396/+288 for floor-alignment exclusions.
claims.Limitations: The resource pointer must be bounded before reproducing this predicate.

claims.Finding: The ASM establishes a third Float32 argument in XMM2. Negative finite frame selects MotionStruct+68; otherwise the explicit frame is forwarded, including NaN. A nonnull motion dispatches vtable+40 with RCX=motion,RDX=matrix,XMM2=frame unless ordered blend+72>0. COMISS/JA also allows unordered blend through. Return AL!=0 yields zero root displacement; otherwise translation and negative atan2f become the root transform.
claims.Limitations: The saved decompiler prototype omits XMM2; it must not define a native call wrapper.

claims.Finding: Finds BAR type9 and stores decoded entry data at MotionStruct+24. Its virtual frame-count and bounds methods are used during animation binding; type16 supplies a separate record.
claims.Limitations: The function is not a safe parser or presence probe: required entry rows are used without bounded-span validation.

claims.Finding: BAR runtime fixup dispatches type9 data to1C5F20, after writing encoded entry pointers.
claims.Limitations: No source-span argument is passed.

claims.Finding: Uses type9 data+144 as RDX, reads its DWORD kind, and dispatches kind0 to1D2610 or kind1 to1DAFB0; other kinds return0.
claims.Limitations: The 144-byte object prefix and payload extent need independent bounds.

claims.Finding: Initializes the common Motion object, sets vtable5B4958 (MotionPrototype0), then calls1A88F0 on a payload-relative table and count difference.
claims.Limitations: Root callback+40 resolves to1DA6A0; constructor side effects are not a validator.

claims.Finding: Initializes the common Motion object and installs vtable5B4A38 (MotionRAW).
claims.Limitations: Root callback+40 resolves to1DB470.

claims.Finding: Stores the supplied payload pointer at Motion+8, installs the base vtable and zeros fields+16..+40.
claims.Limitations: Concrete constructors supply payload=type9+144.

claims.Finding: Prototype root callback initializes identity, reads the root descriptor at payload+DWORD44 and returns1 if descriptor+12 is zero. Otherwise it selects time keys and evaluates up to nine channel curves before rotation/translation/scale composition.
claims.Limitations: Offsets, key counts, frame-rate division and nested curve tables lack a byte-span parameter; all nested parser branches are not yet semantically proven.

claims.Finding: RAW root callback returns identity/1 when payload DWORD44 is zero. Otherwise it computes Float32(frame*rate88)/60, selects two64-byte matrix frames from payload-relative root data, and passes the fractional frame in XMM3 to1DB700.
claims.Limitations: FrameCount36 must be positive and loop-frame84/92 indices must be bounded. Clamp logic alone does not validate counts, negative next indices or spans.

claims.Finding: Matrix interpolation fast path copies the first64-byte matrix for zero fraction. The general path normalizes basis rows, interpolates translation/scales, and rebuilds basis directions using cross products.
claims.Limitations: The complete body is preserved; this claim does not prove all interpolation branches or every exceptional Float32 input.

claims.Finding: Prototype curve evaluation reads payload-relative key/time/value/tangent tables. Wrap branches repeatedly add or subtract the endpoint time span; interpolation divides by the selected time difference.
claims.Limitations: Finite inputs alone do not prove progress: equal endpoint times can make a wrap step zero; repeated Float32 additions can also stop changing a large value. Full curve-schema validation remains open.

claims.Finding: Motion update advances current frame+68, controls blend interval+72, invokes motion callbacks and can bind queued animations while the Actor remains the same.
claims.Limitations: Actor generation alone does not identify a motion resource or projection context.

claims.Finding: Motion rebuild can evaluate model motion during blending, save pose buffers and update native motion bookkeeping.
claims.Limitations: Current Actor matrices do not identify the next animation data to be sampled.

claims.Finding: Copies the supplied matrix into model+696, changes two basis signs, dispatches motion vtable+16 when present, and updates model motion/buffer ownership.
claims.Limitations: Root transform is shared with model evaluation; not a cosmetic-only parameter.

claims.Finding: Selects a tagged animation child and binds it through3C8A40, or clears the motion pointer after cleanup when no child is found.
claims.Limitations: This can change the active motion resource without replacing Actor identity.

claims.Finding: Motion cleanup releases its referenced record, clears handles and linked effects, and invokes an optional callback.
claims.Limitations: No independent monotonic motion epoch is provided by this cleanup.

claims.Finding: Delegates motion cleanup to3C7300 and tail-calls3C7040.
claims.Limitations: Only this delegation is claimed; downstream3C7040 was not freshly reviewed in this round.

abi.rootExtractor: pointer __fastcall(MotionStruct* RCX, float4* RDX, float frame XMM2)
abi.rootCallback: BYTE __fastcall(Motion* RCX, matrix4x4* RDX, float frame XMM2)
abi.rawInterpolate: matrix* __fastcall(matrix* RCX, matrix* RDX, matrix* R8, float fraction XMM3)
abi.basis: Observed register use in full ASM, not saved decompiler prototypes.

next: Bound type9 Motion object and payload against an owned, identified resource span; recognize both exact vtables and root callbacks.
For Prototype, validate channel/key/time/value/tangent ranges and finite arithmetic, including wrap-loop progress, before projecting original/candidate scalars.
For RAW, validate positive frame count, rate/frame arithmetic, both indices and complete matrix spans; reproduce native interpolation in Float32 order.
Validate Euler/direction/floor-alignment branches and changed attachment/axis/ramp context at every commit or restore.
Use actor generation and retained per-owner mutation/cleanup state; finite existing matrices and an acknowledged setter alone are insufficient.
